newsitem.title: USA: Cushing, Okla., fieldhouse vote set for Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Cushing, Okla., fieldhouse vote set for Tuesday.

text.p: Voters Tuesday will decide on the largest bond issue in the Cushing, Okla., public school system's history, a $2.55 million offering for a 2,000-seat high school fieldhouse, the Tulsa World newspaper reported.

The proposed Cushing High School Fieldhouse would total 37,500 square feet, the newspaper said. The project would include a competition-sized basketball court, three full-sized competition wrestling mats, a wrestling practice room, and an indoor walking track for the general public.

Currently, Cushing's only competition-sized basketball facility seats 900, and is located at the middle school gymnasium, two miles from the high school, Superintendent Bill Childress told the newspaper.
"We feel optimistic it will pass," Assistant Superintendent Eddie Williams told Tulsa World. "We're accustomed to our community supporting our school system. We really appreciate that."
If 60 percent of Cushing school district voters approve the bond issue, construction on the new fieldhouse would probably begin on July 1.
